evidence.requirements: Nearly every brief item is implemented. The start page lists title, date/time, price and "<n> seats left" (TastingsPage.tsx:62-73, format.ts:19-22, start.jpg). Each card has a "Book <title>" link (TastingsPage.tsx:85-90). The form has the Name/Email/Guests labels, a 1-8 limit and a "Book" button (BookingPage.tsx:115-173). Errors appear next to the field (form.jpg). The confirmation shows the "Booking confirmed" heading, tasting, guests, total and reference (ConfirmationPage.tsx:54-62, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and a Sign in button, with the password read from STAFF_PASSWORD (StaffPage.tsx:107-131, server/index.ts:5). Bookings are grouped by tasting with a Cancel button that frees seats (StaffPage.tsx:138-197, store.ts:92-102, staff.jpg). Uses React, Express, react-router, react-hook-form, zod and Tailwind, and `npm start` honours PORT (package.json:10-11, index.ts:4). Partly met: (1) a fully booked tasting loses its "Book <title>" control and gets a disabled "Sold out" button instead (TastingsPage.tsx:76-83), which goes against "each tasting has a link or button 'Book <tasting title>'". (2) Each Cancel button's accessible name is overridden to "Cancel booking KB-…" (StaffPage.tsx:182), so it is not a plain "Cancel" button by name. (3) Phone usability is only implied by responsive classes; there is no mobile screenshot.
evidence.correctness: The seat check and the insert run synchronously with no await between them, so concurrent requests cannot oversell (store.ts:25-27, 67-79), and a test covers this (store.test.ts:86-95). Fully booked and not-enough-seats cases return distinct 409s, and the message is singular for one seat (app.ts:60-64). Cancelling deletes the booking from both maps, so its seats come back (store.ts:92-102). Guests are parsed strictly: booleans, arrays, hex and NaN are rejected (booking.ts:17-24, booking.test.ts:61-65). Name and email are trimmed and length-limited. References are unique, generated with crypto.randomInt and retried on collision (store.ts:44-51). Minor: after a 409 the "seats left" text on the booking page is not refreshed (BookingPage.tsx:98). The link to a cancelled booking just shows "Booking not found" rather than saying it was cancelled.
evidence.security: React escapes all output and nothing uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML. The password check compares SHA-256 digests with timingSafeEqual, and sign-in is refused when STAFF_PASSWORD is unset (staff.ts:7-11). Sessions use a 32-byte random token with an 8-hour expiry, sent in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie (app.ts:95-101, staff.ts:14-33). Failed sign-ins are rate-limited (app.ts:74-81), staff routes require a session (app.ts:83-88), and the public confirmation endpoint does not expose the email (api.test.ts:97-105). There are no secrets in the code, and the error handler hides 500 details (app.ts:125-129). Gaps: no sign-out endpoint or button; no security headers or CSP (no helmet); `secure: req.secure` without `trust proxy` means the cookie will not be marked Secure behind a TLS-terminating proxy, and the rate limiter will key every client to the proxy IP.
evidence.code_quality: The structure is small and clear: server/app.ts (routes), store.ts (domain), staff.ts (auth helpers), shared/booking.ts (one zod schema used by client and server), src/api.ts (typed client), and one file per page. Store results are discriminated unions (store.ts:16-20) and page load states are typed (BookingPage.tsx:10). Naming is good and the comments are brief and explain why. The createApp options make the app testable (app.ts:9-13). The only repetition is the same useEffect fetch/cancel pattern on three pages, which react-router loaders could have replaced. It is not a defect.
evidence.tests: Vitest covers both server and client. Supertest API tests (api.test.ts) cover listing, booking, per-field 400s, seat limits, singular wording, fully booked, the confirmation lookup leaking no email, staff auth, cookie flags, grouping, cancel freeing seats, session expiry and rate limiting. There are store unit tests including reference uniqueness, schema boundary tests (booking.test.ts), and Testing Library tests for each page. They check that errors sit next to the right field via aria-describedby (BookingPage.test.tsx:44-53), that a double-click sends one cancel (StaffPage.test.tsx:118-129), and that an ended session returns to sign-in. Weaknesses: every UI test mocks fetch, so no end-to-end test runs the built app. The concurrency test only exercises synchronous calls through microtasks, not real parallel HTTP requests.
evidence.ux_design: The design is coherent and winery-like: deep wine header, cream/parchment cards, serif display font (index.css:3-20, all screenshots). The form error is clear in red under the field with a red border (form.jpg). The confirmation card is clean, with a "Thank you" eyebrow and the reference in monospace (confirmation.jpg). The staff overview is a tidy grouped table with seats left per group and "No bookings yet" (staff.jpg). There are distinct badge colours for plenty, few and fully booked (TastingsPage.tsx:57-59). Issues: start.jpg was captured mid fade-in, so the whole content looks washed out, which shows the 320 ms animation on every route (index.css:32-41, Layout.tsx:25) delays readable content. Cancel runs immediately with no confirmation. There is no sign-out, and the footer still says "Staff sign-in" while signed in. The phone layout is not shown in any screenshot.
evidence.accessibility: Labels are linked with htmlFor/id. Invalid fields get aria-invalid and aria-describedby pointing at the error, and the guests hint is also attached through describedby (BookingPage.tsx:118-164). React Hook Form focuses the first invalid field by default, and form-level errors use role=alert while notices use role=status. There is a skip link, a visible gold focus ring (index.css:27-30) and a reduced-motion override. The staff table has th scope=col and a visually hidden Actions header (StaffPage.tsx:163-169). Muted text (#6b5a5e) on cream has adequate contrast. Gaps: focus is not moved to the new heading after client-side navigation, so the confirmation is not announced. Field errors on the booking form are not live regions. The aria-label on Cancel replaces the visible text, although it still contains it.
evidence.simplicity: The dependency set fits the job: express, express-rate-limit, react, react-router, react-hook-form, zod and Tailwind (package.json:15-24). There is no database, no state library and no extra abstraction layers. The server is about 330 lines across four files and each page is a single component file. One schema serves both client and server.
evidence.maintainability: There is no README, so the repository gives no run, setup or STAFF_PASSWORD instructions; STAFF_PASSWORD is mentioned only in openspec/specs/staff-bookings/spec.md:9 and a console warning (index.ts:7-9). There is no CI pipeline, no .nvmrc or Volta pin (engines is only `>=22`, package.json:7), no changelog or release approach beyond version 1.0.0, no ADRs and no staff manual. On the positive side: the OpenSpec specs document behaviour in detail (openspec/specs/*), package-lock.json is present, there is a typecheck script, the regression tests are solid, and the in-memory trade-off is documented in code (store.ts:25-27). A newcomer would have to reverse-engineer how to run and deploy the app.

unmet_requirements: Fully booked tastings no longer show the "Book <tasting title>" control; it is replaced by a disabled "Sold out" button (TastingsPage.tsx:76-83)
The staff Cancel buttons' accessible name is "Cancel booking KB-…" rather than "Cancel" (StaffPage.tsx:182)
Phone usability is unverified: there are responsive Tailwind classes but no mobile screenshot or test
strengths: Correct, race-free seat accounting with clear server-side 409 handling and one zod schema shared by client and server, so validation is the same in both places (store.ts:67-79, shared/booking.ts)
Solid staff security for the scope: digest-based timingSafeEqual, random session tokens with expiry, HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict cookie, rate-limited sign-in, and refusal when STAFF_PASSWORD is unset
Meaningful API, store, schema and page tests that track the brief closely, plus a polished, coherent winery look with clear error, success and fully booked states
issues: Maintainability gaps: no README with run/setup/STAFF_PASSWORD instructions, no CI pipeline, no Node version pin, no release notes and no staff manual; a new developer or the winery would have to reverse-engineer how to operate it

Staff workflow and session gaps: no sign-out, Cancel runs immediately with no confirmation, and no security headers or `trust proxy` setup, so the cookie is not marked Secure and rate limiting keys every client to the proxy IP when deployed behind TLS

Smaller UX and requirement deviations: fully booked tastings drop the "Book <title>" control, the Cancel accessible name is overridden, the fade-in on every route makes content briefly washed out (start.jpg), and focus is not managed after navigation
review.verdict: A clean, well-tested and attractive React/Express booking app that gets the core rules right: seat limits, validation next to the field, staff auth and cancellation. Before it goes to the winery it needs a README and CI, a sign-out and a cancel confirmation for staff, and proxy-aware cookie and rate-limit settings.
